name: Belgian Dutch (Flemish)
notes: Flemish / Belgian Dutch (Vlaams). Alveolar /r/ [r] in most varieties (vs. NL uvular [ʀ]). /ɣ/ (voiced velar fricative) more robust than in NL Dutch. Considered more conservative than Netherlands Dutch in some features. Strong dialect continuum from West-Flemish to Limburgish. Source: König & van der Auwera (1994). ⟨w⟩ (Verhoeven 2005, JIPA 35(2)): "[w] has a labial-velar articulation rather than labiodental in many accents of Netherlandic Dutch" (p. 245), with "w waːʀ̥ waar 'true'" in the word list (p. 244). So ⟨w⟩ is [w], against the [ʋ] of nl-NL, and the consonant that ⟨ieuw eeuw uw⟩ give before a vowel is [w] too: leeuwen [leːwən], nieuwe [niwə], duwen [dywən]. Paardekooper (1987, ABN-uitspraakgids, p. XVIII) notes the same bilabial w "in veel zuidelijke dialecten". ⟨g ch⟩ (Verhoeven 2005, p. 244): "Belgian Dutch has a voiced and voiceless velar fricative: these are absent in the Netherlands", with "x xɛil chijl" and "ɣ ɣɛil geil" in the word list. So nl-BE restates the velar values of ⟨g ch sch berg brecht⟩ against the uvular [χ] of nl-NL. ⟨ee eu oo⟩ and the open-syllable ⟨e o⟩ (Verhoeven 2005, pp. 245-246): "In Belgian Dutch, however, they are always monophthongs". So nl-BE disables the six NL_MID_TENSE_* rules by id and keeps [eː øː oː] against the closing diphthongs [ei øy ou] of nl-NL. ⟨r⟩ (Verhoeven 2005, p. 245): "The alveolar trill is most frequent and geographically most widely distributed", and the trill is voiceless "word-finally as in [doːʀ̥] 'through' and when followed by a voiceless stop in consonant clusters as in [vaːʀ̥t] 'sails'". So nl-BE disables the coda [ɹ] of nl-NL, keeps the trill [r] and devoices it word-finally and before /p t k/ (NL_BE_R_DEVOICE_*). The key ⟨kerk⟩ states [r̥] itself, because the rules do not reach inside a key of more than one segment. ONSET ⟨v z g⟩: nl-BE keeps the voiced [v z ɣ]. Verhoeven (2005, p. 244) states the category: "Belgian Dutch has a voiced and voiceless velar fricative". The measurements give a gradient share. The same page: "70% of word-initial and 56% of intervocalic fricatives are realised without any trace of vocal fold vibration". Verhoeven & Hageman (2007, Nederlandse Taalkunde 12(2)) measured 4,800 tokens of 40 speakers from four Flemish regions: 16% of the fricatives fully voiced, 17% partly devoiced and 65% fully devoiced, with a mean voicing of 16% for /ɣ/, 30% for /v/ and 32% for /z/ (p. 143); 20% voicing word-initially against 32% word-internally, and "geen significante verschillen tussen de regio’s" (p. 144); 84% of the fricatives "(geheel of gedeeltelijk) zonder stembandtrilling" (p. 145). They also report Van de Velde & Van Hout (2001), which is cited here only as they report it: 56% of the Flemish fricatives sound voiced (p. 139), and listeners judge only 61.24% of the fricatives as devoiced (p. 145). van der Harst & Van de Velde (2007, Taal en Tongval 59, p. 184, Table 4): the word-initial (γ) of guize is fully voiceless in 86.3% of the Flemish teacher tokens, and in 95.0% in Flemish Brabant. The category claim and the measured shares conflict, and no opened source states a categorical [f s x] for the onset, so the spec keeps the voiced values. DOUBLED CONSONANT LETTERS (collapse_geminates): a doubled consonant letter spells one consonant, and two identical consonants that meet inside the word are one. The flag is not inherited, so the spec states it, as nl-NL and its children do. Verhoeven (2005, JIPA 35(2), p. 247) transcribes the Belgian Standard Dutch reading with one consonant for each doubled letter: uittrekken [ʔœytrɛkə], induffelde [ɪndʏfəldə], onmiddellijk [ɔmɪdələk]. CODA DEVOICING INSIDE ⟨berg⟩ AND ⟨veld⟩: Paardekooper (1987, ABN-uitspraakgids) transcribes the Belgian norm (p. V: the ABN form matters "vooral voor Vlaanderen"). He writes the devoiced obstruent both at the end of a compound member and before a voiceless obstruent inside the word: bergketen bɛr ə xketə and bergplaats bɛr ə xplats (p. 21), gebergte gə'bɛr ə xtə (p. 69), veldpost vɛltpɔst and veldslag vɛltslɑx (p. 218). He gives no rule in words. ⟨berg⟩ and ⟨veld⟩ are one grapheme slot each, so NL_BE_CODA_DEVOICE_BERG and NL_CODA_DEVOICE_VELD match the whole slot before a voiceless obstruent: bergtop [ˈbɛrxtɔp], gebergte [ɣəˈbɛrxtə], veldslag [ˈvɛltslɑx]. LEAD, NOT MODELLED: Paardekooper writes a svarabhakti schwa in the coda clusters ⟨rg rk lk⟩ (berg bɛr ə x, berk bɛr ə k, balk bɑl ə k). Inside one morpheme he writes it in almost every headword. The two coda exceptions found are bewerkstelligen bə'werkstɛləgə (p. 24) and overwerk ovərwɛrk (p. 148), against achterwerk ɑxtərwɛr ə k (p. 5). Where the letters span a morpheme boundary (verklaren, overgroot, taalkring) he writes no schwa, because the cluster is no coda there. ⟨qu⟩ is [kw], against the [kʋ] of nl-NL. Paardekooper (1987, p. 164) writes kw (quota kwota), and the w of this spec is [w] (Verhoeven 2005, p. 245). The French loans with plain [k] come from NL_QU_FRENCH_K of nl-NL. The prefixed words bevel, gestel, gezel and gezwel are word exceptions with the stress after the prefix (Paardekooper 1987, pp. 23, 73, 74, 75): the schwa-rime test of nl-NL would put the stress on the prefix.

allophone_rules.notes: Verhoeven (2005, JIPA 35(2), pp. 245-246): "The main difference between Belgian Dutch and Netherlandic Dutch has to do with the pronunciation of the half-close long vowels [eː], [øː] and [oː]. In the Netherlands, these are frequently diphthongized. In Belgian Dutch, however, they are always monophthongs." So nl-BE disables the inherited nl-NL rule and keeps the monophthong.

Disabled: the coda approximant [ɹ] is Netherlandic (Gussenhoven 1992, p. 46). Verhoeven (2005, JIPA 35(2), p. 245): "The alveolar trill is most frequent and geographically most widely distributed." and "The alveolar/uvular trill is voiced in all positions, except word-finally as in [doːʀ̥] 'through' and when followed by a voiceless stop in consonant clusters as in [vaːʀ̥t] 'sails'."

⟨veld⟩ is one grapheme slot, and the inherited NL_CODA_DEVOICE_D names the grapheme ⟨d⟩, so it does not reach the [d] of the slot. This rule names the grapheme ⟨veld⟩ and devoices the last segment of the slot. Paardekooper (1987, ABN-uitspraakgids) transcribes the Belgian norm (p. V: the ABN form matters "vooral voor Vlaanderen"). He writes the devoiced obstruent both at the end of a compound member and before a voiceless obstruent inside the word: bergketen bɛr ə xketə and bergplaats bɛr ə xplats (p. 21), gebergte gə'bɛr ə xtə (p. 69), veldpost vɛltpɔst and veldslag vɛltslɑx (p. 218). He gives no rule in words. Before a vowel the [d] is an onset and stays: velden [ˈvɛldən]. Before /b d/ the rule leaves it voiced: veldbed vɛl(d)bɛt (p. 218).

⟨berg⟩ is one grapheme slot, and the inherited NL_CODA_DEVOICE_G names the grapheme ⟨g⟩, so it does not reach the [ɣ] of the slot. This rule names the grapheme ⟨berg⟩ and devoices the last segment of the slot. The word-final [x] comes from positional_graphemes. Paardekooper (1987, ABN-uitspraakgids) transcribes the Belgian norm (p. V: the ABN form matters "vooral voor Vlaanderen"). He writes the devoiced obstruent both at the end of a compound member and before a voiceless obstruent inside the word: bergketen bɛr ə xketə and bergplaats bɛr ə xplats (p. 21), gebergte gə'bɛr ə xtə (p. 69), veldpost vɛltpɔst and veldslag vɛltslɑx (p. 218). He gives no rule in words. So bergtop is [ˈbɛrxtɔp] and gebergte [ɣəˈbɛrxtə]. Before a vowel the [ɣ] stays: bergen bɛr ə gə (p. 21). His svarabhakti schwa (bɛr ə x) is not modelled. nl-BE-x-antwerp gives the slot its own value [bɛɾəɣ], and this rule devoices its last segment too: bergtop [ˈbɛɾəxtɔp].

Verhoeven (2005, JIPA 35(2), p. 245): "The alveolar trill is most frequent and geographically most widely distributed." and "The alveolar/uvular trill is voiced in all positions, except word-finally as in [doːʀ̥] 'through' and when followed by a voiceless stop in consonant clusters as in [vaːʀ̥t] 'sails'." So a word-final /r/ is the voiceless trill: door [doːr̥].

Verhoeven (2005, JIPA 35(2), p. 245): "The alveolar trill is most frequent and geographically most widely distributed." and "The alveolar/uvular trill is voiced in all positions, except word-finally as in [doːʀ̥] 'through' and when followed by a voiceless stop in consonant clusters as in [vaːʀ̥t] 'sails'." So /r/ before /p t k/ is the voiceless trill: vaart [vaːr̥t], dorp [dɔr̥p].
